thread:
Priya: preflight handoff — I'm primary until 12:00 UTC. Short morning summary + what to watch for.

IncidentBot: PAGER: 2 active incidents overnight: INC5201 (kv-cache eviction burst), INC5202 (autoscaler oscillation). Links: https://pd.redwood/INC5201 https://pd.redwood/INC5202

Jonah: Quick context — around 02:45 UTC a misbehaving tenant sent very large embed batches which coincided with a redis leader election. Evictions spiked and the autoscaler reacted to pod CPU/memory churn causing scale thrash.

Mei: Dashboards & logs to watch: /d/kv-eviction, /d/autoscaler-events, /d/batcher-latency. Sample logs (sanitized):
```
W 02:46:01 kvcache/replica evictions=278 leader_change=true
E 02:46:12 batcher/worker mem_rss=2.9Gi queue_len=640
I 02:47:03 autoscaler/ctrl cooldown=15s decision=scale_down_then_up
```

Priya: What we did overnight
- Temporarily reduced batcher.max_batch_size to 56 for noisy tenants via tenant-config.
- Increased batcher pool memory by 1Gi for the affected fleet (rollout done).
- Pinned kv-cache replicas to improve AZ distribution and reduced leader election risk.
- Rolled back the experimental autoscaler rule that used per-pod RSS spikes as an immediate scale signal.

OpsBot: CI: hotfix branch autoscaler-debounce created, PR #5017. Canary started in staging.

Jonah: Current customer impact
- Roughly 0.7% of global requests saw p95 degradation during the window; two medium customers had transient 502s. No data integrity issues. No SLA breach currently.

Priya: Open action items
1) Autoscaler debounce patch merge + prod canary (PR #5017) — assignee: Mei
2) Runbook: add a section to explicitly call out "when to tenant-rate-limit" (runbook PR queued) — assignee: Jonah
3) Infra ticket to verify redis anti-affinity and pod eviction drains (INF-1302) — assignee: oncall-manager

Mei: Quick ops commands (copy/paste safe)
```
# temporarily limit tenant batch size
curl -X POST https://api.redwood/tenants/tenant-99/config -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_OPS" -d '{"batch_size":56}'

# route override to low-latency model for affected routes
curl -X POST https://api.redwood/ops/route/override -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_OPS" -d '{"route":"low-latency","duration":600}'
```

Priya: Handoff state
- INC5201 (kv evictions) trending down; still open. INC5202 (autoscaler) noisy until debounce patch validated.
- No rollbacks planned; prefer to validate canary then promote.

oncall-manager: Coverage note — Priya primary until 12:00 UTC, Jonah secondary. After 12:00 UTC Mei primary and Priya secondary. There is a 3-hour APAC-gap window (UTC 22:00-01:00 local APAC) flagged — recommend arranging a temporary APAC backup or enable stricter tenant throttles before that window.

Priya: Customer comms
- No public status update yet. If any top-10 tenant sees >5% error rate for >15m, we will send a targeted update and loop in @support_lead.

Mei: Night team checklist if you take over early
- Watch /d/autoscaler-events for oscillation; if it resumes after patch, revert to stable cooldown and open INF-1302 with attached metrics.
- If batcher.queue_len > 500 for 10+ minutes, apply tenant rate-limits and route override to low-latency.
- If kv evictions >200 in a 5m window, escalate to INF-1302 and pin replicas to different AZs.

Jonah: I'll finish the runbook edits and add an example incident table.

Priya: Wrapping up — I'll publish a short blameless post-incident note after the autoscaler canary is promoted. If anyone takes over early, drop your name/time here. :thumbsup:
